title: overlap-aware-kvcache-routing-and-prefill-throttling
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Introduce overlap-aware KV cache routing and a prefill throttling mechanism to reduce hotspot contention and improve tail latency under high concurrent prefill loads. No API changes.
description: Motivation: When aggressive speculative prefill and chunked prefill are enabled we observed KV-cache write hot spots and contention on a subset of worker shards. This manifests as elevated p99 decode latency during high-concurrency prefill bursts. This PR introduces two coordinated changes: 1) an overlap-aware KV-cache routing layer that routes prefill writes to a rotatable set of shards to avoid single-shard hotspots, and 2) a prefill throttling token-bucket that smooths bursty prefill scheduling while still allowing decode overlap. Design: - KV routing: annotate prefill chunks with a routing token derived from request id + chunk index; use lightweight consistent-rotor that prefers local shard but rotates under load. This is implemented as a pluggable Router trait so future strategies (e.g., model-aware hashing) can be added. - Prefill throttling: per-worker token bucket with adjustable refill rate and burst capacity. Prefill scheduler consults token bucket before scheduling chunk prefill; decode stage has a higher priority lane and can borrow tokens for immediate low-latency decode when necessary. - Overlap heuristics: a short-lived 'overlap window' (ms configurable) allows prefill and decode to run concurrently; if the token bucket is exhausted the scheduler will fall back to staggered prefill that prioritizes decode continuity. Implementation summary: - runtime/scheduler/prefill_router.rs: new Router trait and Rotor implementation (approx 180 LOC). - runtime/scheduler/prefill_throttle.rs: token-bucket + metrics hooks (120 LOC). - runtime/kv_cache/shard_writer.rs: minor changes to accept routing token and perform non-blocking handoff. - runtime/executor/overlap_controller.rs: integration glue and configuration flags. - tests/runtime/bench_overlap.rs: microbench harness for p50/p95/p99 under synthetic load. - e2e/ci/prefill_integration.test: integration asserts for correctness and no cache corruption. Backwards compatibility: router defaults to previous behavior when disabled; default config keeps prefill enabled but conservative throttle parameters. Rollout plan: staged feature flag enabled on canary pool then ramp to production over 72 hours with metrics monitoring (kv_write_conflicts, prefill_retries, p99_decode_latency). Checklist: - [x] unit tests for routing and token-bucket - [x] integration tests for decode correctness - [x] microbench numbers attached - [x] docs: config knobs documented in ops/configs.md - [x] metrics and dashboard PR queued

review_comments: Arjun: Can you justify why rotor-based routing is better than deterministic hashing in high churn? Response: rotor keeps affinity but rotates under pressure; deterministic hashing caused permanent hot shards on skewed request ids.
Lena: Suggest adding a metric for token-bucket drained events. Response: added prefill_throttle.drained_count and export in metrics.
Diego: Concern about additional allocations in hot path. Response: optimized Router to use stack-allocated small buffer and re-used rotor state; microbench shows minimal overhead.
Arjun: Please add a short runbook entry in ops for throttle tuning. Response: added to ops/configs.md with recommended knobs for small/medium/large clusters.
bench_results: Synthetic concurrent prefill workload (2000 concurrent streams): p50 latency improved 8%, p95 improved 12%, p99 improved 22% after enabling rotor routing + throttle (throttle conservative config).
Hotspot test (single-request-id skew): prior p99 spikes to 1.2s, new routing reduces peak to 420ms with same hardware and kernel versions.
Throughput: end-to-end token/sec unchanged (+/- 2%) under sustained load; decode tail improved due to less prefill contention.
notes: Feature gated behind runtime.feature.overlap_prefill (default enabled on canary).
Ops knobs: prefill_throttle.refill_rate, prefill_throttle.burst, overlap_window_ms. Start with recommended values in ops/configs.md.
Rollback: feature flag off or throttle refilled to high value to mimic legacy behaviour. No schema changes to persisted cache layout.
Follow-ups: explore model-aware routing and estimate-driven token allocation per model size.
